issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation 'ngồi ăn' (sitting eating) interprets 'κατακειμενον' (katakeimenon) as sitting/lying down to eat, whereas the Greek 'κατακειμενον' specifically means 'lying down'. More importantly, 'εσθιειν' (estiein) is an infinitive modifying the purpose of the construction; the Vietnamese 'được xây dựng để ăn' suggests a passive result or purpose that slightly shifts the rhetorical structure of the Greek 'οικοδομηθησεται εις το... εσθιειν'.

The Vietnamese translation adds 'há chẳng' (rhetorical question marker), which is a stylistic choice to mirror the rhetorical tone of the Greek, but it slightly alters the directness of the Greek construction.
